runs.name: case_counts_60
runs.note: Count bootstrap + naive on the 36/12/12 split, two test origins (2026-04-30, 2026-05-30), 300 paths.
runs.conclusion: Count prediction improved over naive while cumulative cash flow got worse (ratio 1.259 unseen), which motivated evaluating full event generators instead of counts alone.

runs.name: event_models_2_origins
runs.note: Five event generators vs naive, gbm_global, ensemble and the count bootstrap on the same two origins, 300 paths.
runs.conclusion: Blocks and hybrid had the lowest cumulative net-flow error; renewal and the GRU did not; with only 18 unseen origins the differences were not yet trustworthy.

runs.name: event_adjust_11_origins_pooled
runs.note: Month-end origins 2025-07..2026-05; eight in-sample dates and three out-of-fit dates pooled. Includes mixture and spread variants.
runs.conclusion: Pooled rows mix in-sample and out-of-fit windows; kept for comparison, not for claims. Spread calibration was fitted here on 20 calibration company-origins.

runs.name: event_adjust_11_origins_out_of_fit
runs.note: Only the out-of-fit origins 2026-03-31, 2026-04-30 and 2026-05-31 (27 unseen company-origins, 9 companies, 6 gap events).
runs.conclusion: Headline comparison. Blocks is best by point estimate (0.784 vs naive), three models keep their bootstrap interval below parity with the ensemble, mixture adds nothing, one-scalar spread calibration failed for blocks, and gap probabilities are uncalibrated.

cohorts.unseen: Companies never used to fit the model (test companies from the count reference). Out-of-fit benchmarks additionally require the 30-day target window to end after the fit cutoff.
cohorts.seen_future: The same companies the models were fitted on, evaluated at later dates. This measures temporal robustness only and is in-sample by company; do not present it as generalization.

metrics.net_mae_vs_naive: Ratio of cumulative net-flow MAE to seasonal naive on identical origins. Below 1 means better than naive; the only cross-model number comparable within a cohort.
metrics.net_path_mae: Mean absolute error of cumulative net flow in rubles, averaged over days and origins.
metrics.flow_wape: Pooled weighted absolute percentage error of daily gross inflow/outflow; not comparable with balance-relative WAPE.
metrics.business_path_wape: Path error relative to the business balance magnitude.
metrics.net_coverage: Share of actual cumulative net flow inside the predicted p10-p90 band; nominal target 0.80. Higher is not automatically better: 0.98 means intervals are too wide.
metrics.net_width: Mean p10-p90 span in rubles; read together with coverage.
metrics.net_pinball: Quantile (pinball) loss in rubles across p10/p50/p90.
metrics.gap_brier: Brier score of the probability that the business balance drops below zero within 30 days.
metrics.gap_precision_0.5: Gap alarm metrics at probability threshold 0.5; also available at 0.3 and 0.1. Accuracy is dominated by the negative class and should be read with the base rate.
metrics.flow_mse: Mean squared daily gross-flow error, in rubles squared.
metrics.net_mse: Mean squared cumulative net-flow error, in rubles squared.
metrics.count_crps: Empirical-sample CRPS of daily transaction counts; only defined for event generators, null for aggregate models.
metrics.marked_count_crps: CRPS of direction-by-category counts per day; event generators only.
metrics.amount_bin_count_crps: CRPS of direction-by-amount-bin counts per day, including an exact-zero bin and an unbounded upper tail; event generators only.

caveats: All runs use the synthetic case corpus, which was explored during earlier development; none is an independent external audit.
The unseen cohort is small (9-12 companies), and out-of-fit gap metrics rest on about six events.
Month-end origins produce overlapping 30-day windows that share future data, so company-origin rows are correlated; bootstrap intervals are approximate.
Origins whose window ends on or before the 2026-03-31 fit cutoff are in-sample. Use the *_out_of_fit benchmark for headline comparisons.
Gap probabilities over-predict out-of-fit and have negative Brier skill versus a constant base-rate forecast; they are not calibrated.
Aggregate models (naive, gbm_global, ensemble) have no count or marked-event outputs, so their event rows are null rather than zero.
No transformer checkpoint was trained or compared in these runs; research code is not on the serving path.

note: Values are copied from completed runs; see each run's metadata.json for config, split and hashes. Cohorts differ between benchmarks and must not be pooled.
